metadata.name: fleet
metadata.description: Safe, rolling maintenance for small fleets: apt upgrades over flaky SSH paths, one-node-at-a-time k3s reboots, and guarded podman-compose stack updates.

collection_readme.name: README.md
collection_readme.html:
iacker.fleet

Rolling maintenance for small fleets, written for a real one: a three-node k3s cluster reached over Tailscale and a cloud VM running a podman-compose stack that other people use during the day.

Each role does one job and refuses to continue when the situation is unsafe.

Role What it does Main guard
apt_upgrade Upgrades packages, never reboots, sets apt_upgrade_reboot_required apt runs detached (async), so an upgrade of the VPN that carries SSH cannot kill dpkg halfway
k3s_rolling_reboot preflight: every node Ready. main: cordon, reboot, wait Ready, uncordon stops the whole run on the first failure and prints the exact uncordon command
podman_compose_update Backs up, pulls, recreates, waits for healthy containers, prunes, checks URLs refuses to pull without enough free disk

Install

ansible-galaxy collection install iacker.fleet

Requires ansible-core 2.18+ and kubectl on the controller for k3s_rolling_reboot.

Rolling OS update of a k3s cluster

- name: Preflight
  hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: iacker.fleet.k3s_rolling_reboot
        tasks_from: preflight

- name: Agents first, one at a time
  hosts: k3s_agents
  serial: 1
  any_errors_fatal: true
  become: true
  roles:
    - iacker.fleet.apt_upgrade
    - iacker.fleet.k3s_rolling_reboot

- name: Server last
  hosts: k3s_server
  serial: 1
  any_errors_fatal: true
  become: true
  roles:
    - iacker.fleet.apt_upgrade
    - iacker.fleet.k3s_rolling_reboot

Nodes reboot only when the OS asks for it (/var/run/reboot-required), or with -e k3s_rolling_reboot_force=true. Set k3s_rolling_reboot_node_name in host_vars when the Kubernetes node name differs from the inventory name.

Why drain is off by default. On a small cluster, draining the big node pushes its heavy pods onto the smallest one, which then thrashes, and local-path volumes cannot move anyway. Cordon plus a two-minute reboot lets pods restart in place. Turn it on with k3s_rolling_reboot_drain: true when you have the headroom.

Updating a podman-compose stack

- hosts: app_vm
  roles:
    - role: iacker.fleet.podman_compose_update
      vars:
        podman_compose_update_project_dir: /home/app/stack
        podman_compose_update_project_name: app
        podman_compose_update_systemd_unit: app-stack
        podman_compose_update_backup_files: [compose.yml, .env, /home/app/data/app.db]
        podman_compose_update_expected_containers: [app_web_1, app_api_1]
        podman_compose_update_health_commands:
          - { name: api, cmd: "podman exec app_web_1 curl -fsS http://api:8080/health", expect: ok }
        podman_compose_update_url_checks:
          - { url: "https://app.example.com/", status: [200] }

Back up the database of any service that migrates its schema on start: without it, rolling back to the old image is not possible.

Testing

CI runs ansible-lint (production profile), ansible-test sanity, builds the collection, and runs apt_upgrade and podman_compose_update for real on a GitHub runner. k3s_rolling_reboot is exercised in check mode on a live cluster before each release; rebooting CI runners is not possible.

contents.readme_html:
iacker.fleet.apt_upgrade

Entry point main

Upgrade packages, never reboot, report whether a reboot is needed.

  • Runs an apt upgrade detached from the SSH session (async), keeps local config files.
  • Sets the fact apt_upgrade_reboot_required for a later reboot role.
Variable Type Default Description
apt_upgrade_type str "dist" Value passed to the upgrade option of ansible.builtin.apt.
apt_upgrade_autoremove bool true Remove packages that are no longer needed.
apt_upgrade_cache_valid_time int 3600 Skip apt update if the cache is younger than this (seconds).
apt_upgrade_async int 1800 Maximum runtime of the detached upgrade (seconds). 0 runs it synchronously.
apt_upgrade_poll int 10 Polling interval for the detached upgrade (seconds).

See the collection README for complete playbooks.

iacker.fleet.k3s_rolling_reboot

Entry point main

Reboot one k3s node safely (cordon, optional drain, Ready wait, uncordon).

  • Meant to run with serial: 1 and any_errors_fatal: true.
  • kubectl commands are delegated to the controller.
  • On failure the play stops and prints the exact uncordon command.
Variable Type Default Description
k3s_rolling_reboot_kubectl str "kubectl" kubectl command on the controller, for example kubectl --context prod.
k3s_rolling_reboot_node_name str "{{ inventory_hostname }}" Kubernetes node name, when it differs from the inventory name.
k3s_rolling_reboot_needed bool "{{ apt_upgrade_reboot_required \| default(false) }}" Whether the node needs a reboot. Defaults to the fact set by iacker.fleet.apt_upgrade.
k3s_rolling_reboot_force bool false Reboot even if no reboot is required.
k3s_rolling_reboot_drain bool false Drain before rebooting. Off by default, see README.
k3s_rolling_reboot_drain_timeout str "300s" Timeout passed to kubectl drain.
k3s_rolling_reboot_timeout int 900 Maximum time to wait for the node to come back over SSH (seconds).
k3s_rolling_reboot_ready_retries int 30 Attempts while waiting for the node to be Ready.
k3s_rolling_reboot_ready_delay int 10 Seconds between Ready checks.

Entry point preflight

Fail unless every node of the cluster is Ready. Run on the controller.

Variable Type Default Description
k3s_rolling_reboot_kubectl str "kubectl" kubectl command on the controller.

See the collection README for complete playbooks.

iacker.fleet.podman_compose_update

Entry point main

Pull and recreate a podman-compose stack, refusing to fill the disk.

  • Checks free space before pulling, backs up files, recreates the stack (through its user systemd unit or podman-compose), waits for the expected containers, prunes replaced images, then runs health and URL checks.
Variable Type Default Description
podman_compose_update_project_dir path required Directory holding the compose file.
podman_compose_update_compose_file str "compose.yml" Compose file name, relative to the project directory.
podman_compose_update_project_name str "" Compose project name (-p). Empty uses the podman-compose default.
podman_compose_update_systemd_unit str "" User systemd unit running the stack. Empty recreates with up -d --force-recreate.
podman_compose_update_backup_files list ["{{ podman_compose_update_compose_file }}"] Files to back up as <file>.bak.<timestamp>. Relative paths start at the project directory.
podman_compose_update_min_free_gb int 8 Minimum free space (GB) required before pulling.
podman_compose_update_free_space_path str "" Path whose filesystem is measured. Empty uses the podman image store (graphRoot).
podman_compose_update_prune_images bool true Prune dangling images before and after the update.
podman_compose_update_journal_vacuum_size str "" Cap the systemd journal to this size first (needs become). Empty skips it.
podman_compose_update_pull_timeout int 1800 Maximum pull time (seconds).
podman_compose_update_expected_containers list [] Container names that must be running and not starting/unhealthy.
podman_compose_update_wait_retries int 30 Attempts while waiting for containers.
podman_compose_update_wait_delay int 10 Seconds between attempts.
podman_compose_update_health_commands list [] Commands run on the host after the update, as name, cmd, expect (substring of stdout).
podman_compose_update_url_checks list [] URLs checked from the controller, as url and status (list of accepted codes).

See the collection README for complete playbooks.
